title: Companion Mode on Mac: One Login for the App and CLI
summary: Pangolin for macOS 0.14 and CLI 0.23 bring companion mode to Mac. Sign in and connect in the desktop app, then run CLI commands as that same account.
body_markdown:
On Windows and Linux, Pangolin CLI already shares a login and tunnel with the desktop app through companion mode. On Mac, the app and CLI were separate: you signed into each on its own, and the CLI ran its own tunnel. That made using them together awkward. You could be logged into one account in the menu bar app and a different account in the CLI, or have a different organization selected in each, so a command like` pangolin ssh` might hit the wrong account or org even though the desktop app looked correct. Keeping both in sync was something you had to do by hand.


Pangolin for macOS 0.14 and Pangolin CLI 0.23 fix this problem. Companion mode on Mac works the same way it does on the other desktop platforms: log in and connect in the app once, then use the CLI as that same account.


## Why Companion Mode


Plenty of people keep the Mac client connected all day and still want the CLI for SSH, SCP, and other commands. Two logins meant two places to switch organizations or exit nodes, and two places that could drift out of sync. Companion mode puts the desktop app in charge of identity and the tunnel, so the CLI is just another way to use the connection you already have.


## How It Works


Companion mode is on by default once both the Mac app (0.14.0 or later) and the CLI (0.23.0 or later) are installed.


1. Log in with the Mac client and connect.
2. Install Pangolin CLI if you need it: from the menu bar, choose **More** > **Install Pangolin CLI…** , or use the[CLI install steps](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/clients/platforms/cli#install) . The app installs the CLI to` /usr/local/bin/pangolin` .
3. Run CLI commands in a terminal. For example:


```text
pangolin ssh username@ alias


```


The CLI follows the account, organization, and exit node selected in the desktop app. Change those in the app. While companion mode is on,` pangolin login` ,` pangolin logout` , and` pangolin select` for account, organization, or exit node are blocked.


The desktop app has to be open and logged in. If it isn't, the CLI asks you to start Pangolin and log in. Check status or turn companion mode off with:


```text
pangolin companion status
pangolin companion  disable


```


Turn it back on later with` pangolin companion enable` . On machines without the desktop app, the CLI keeps its own login and can start its own tunnel as before.


Details are in the[Mac companion mode](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/clients/platforms/mac#companion-mode) and[CLI companion mode](https://docs.pangolin.net/manage/clients/platforms/cli#companion-mode) docs. Update from[Downloads](https://pangolin.net/downloads) or check for updates in the Mac app under **More** > **Check for Updates…** .
